issues.description: The problem statement requires a Bookstore initializer with the signature init(books: [Book]) (problem_statement.md). In the solution, Bookstore is declared with an extra parameter init(books: [Book], valid: Bool) (Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift), but the solution's Client calls Bookstore(books: books) (Sources/BookstoreLib/Client.swift). This creates a structural mismatch between the specification and the solution and an internal inconsistency in the solution that would prevent successful compilation and confuse students about the correct constructor signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Bookstore initializer match the problem specification by changing the solution to init(books: [Book]) and remove the unused 'valid: Bool' parameter. Alternatively, if the extra parameter is intentional, update the problem statement and all call sites (e.g. Client) to use the new signature and document the purpose of the parameter. The preferred fix is to remove the extra parameter so the initializer matches init(books: [Book]).

issues.description: The Problem Statement requires a Bookstore initializer with signature init(books: [Book]), but the solution's Bookstore implementation declares init(books: [Book], valid: Bool). This extra parameter name ('valid') in the solution diverges from the described API and from the assembleBookstore usage (which calls Bookstore(books: books)), creating confusion about the intended initializer and causing a mismatch students must reconcile.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Bookstore initializer match the problem statement and template usage by removing the extraneous parameter. Change the solution initializer to init(books: [Book]) and update any internal calls accordingly (or, if an extra parameter is required, document and reflect it consistently in the problem statement and template).
